key_insight: An agentic workflow can convert published neutral-atom quantum ideas into overnight QPU experiments, but expert review remains essential to catch scientific and hardware-level mistakes.
engineering_relevance: This lowers the barrier to running quantum hardware campaigns by automating protocol translation, compilation, simulation, and cloud execution for neutral-atom processors.
method: Agent plans and executes the end-to-end quantum workflow on cloud-accessible Pasqal QPUs.
Human researcher validates critical steps to preserve scientific correctness.
A second agent screens 633 Rydberg-array arXiv papers for current hardware feasibility and upgrade needs.
evidence_signal: In three case studies, the agent moved from a published paper or patent to an overnight QPU campaign, and in a corpus of 633 papers it found nearly half appear implementable on present-day QPUs.
watch_item: The workflow can produce plausible but incorrect choices or diagnoses, so expert oversight is required before trusting results.
paper_title: Lowering the implementation barrier of neutral-atom quantum computing with agentic workflows
